initial_prompts: Use case: identity-preserve. Asset type: production walking sprite atlas for a Godot 2D mobile horde survival game. The attached roster is a reference for character identity and pixel-art style. Use ONLY the FIRST character, the hooded female hunter, preserving her dark purple hood and short cloak, burgundy scarf, pale face and blond fringe, simple boots, and tiny warm amber charm. EMPTY HANDS, no integrated weapon. Create a genuine EIGHT-FRAME WALK CYCLE with clearly changing leg positions, alternating feet lifting and planting, gentle opposing arm swing, flowing scarf and cloak trailing the step, consistent silhouette and proportions. All frames face RIGHT in the same slightly top-down three-quarter gameplay view, NOT different viewing directions. Composition is a precise uniform grid of FOUR COLUMNS by TWO ROWS, eight equal SQUARE cells, no gutters; reading order left-to-right then next row is frames 1 through 8 of ONE seamless walking cycle. Aim for a 1536x768 canvas (384x384 cells). Each frame's character has the same scale and center; body about 70% cell height, ground baseline exactly at 85% cell height, horizontal body pivot at 50% cell width. Maintain identical head size and torso proportions across frames. Keep feet and cloak well inside each cell with transparent margins so animation frames never overlap neighboring cells. The feet must actually walk, do not just duplicate and tilt an identical static drawing. Low-resolution chunky pixel art equivalent to a 40x48 sprite enlarged with nearest-neighbor edges, simple deliberate square pixel clusters, 8-12 colors, sharp pixels, restrained shading. Genuine transparent background. No text, no labels, no borders, no grid lines, no scenery, no ground shadows, no checkerboard, no weapons, no extra characters. Do not include any monsters from the reference.

Use case: identity-preserve. Asset type: production monster animation atlas for a Godot 2D mobile horde survival game. The attached roster is a visual identity reference. Preserve the FOUR monsters and their dark purple, bone and ember palette. Create one precisely aligned sheet with SIX COLUMNS and FOUR ROWS, 24 equal SQUARE cells, no gutters. Aim for a 1536x1024 canvas (256x256 cells). Row 1: the SMALL SHADOW CRAWLER, two amber eyes, short clawed legs, a six-frame scuttling walk with alternating legs. Row 2: the FLOATING SINGLE EYE with burgundy tendrils, a six-frame seamless hovering cycle where tendrils curl and uncurl and the soft body pulses. Row 3: the LEAN HORNED BONE BEAST, a six-frame stalking/running walk with alternating legs and moving long clawed arms. Row 4: the BULKY ARMORED COLOSSUS with bony shoulders and amber chest crack, a six-frame heavy deliberate walk with alternating planted feet and weight shifting shoulders. Each row contains the SAME character across all six cells, in the same consistent facing-RIGHT slightly top-down three-quarter gameplay view. Do NOT rotate the character to other directions. Each row's anatomy, size, costume, head position and palette must remain consistent between frames. Animate internal limb motion rather than repeating one static pose. Within every cell keep the body's horizontal pivot at 50% cell width and ground baseline at 85% cell height; monsters are approximately 65-72% cell height with plenty of transparent padding. Eye row shares the same body anchor while tentacles move. No sprite can touch or cross a cell edge. Match the reference's simple low-resolution pixel style, around 32x40 logical pixels per small monster, 48x48 for brute, enlarged sharp square clusters, minimal flat shading, no gradients, no painterly detail. Genuinely transparent background, no ground, no shadows, no grid lines, no labels, no text, no borders, no extra objects, no hunter.
refinement_prompts: Edit target: attached 4-column by 2-row hunter animation atlas. Keep the exact character identity, palette, pixel-art rendering, facing right, eight cells, transparency and the same canvas layout. Change ONLY the WALKING POSES, especially LEGS. The previous sheet repeats a wide-legged pose; this edit MUST have dramatic, clearly different foot positions across the cycle, including NARROW feet-together passing poses. Frames 1 and 5 are WIDE CONTACT poses with opposite feet forward. Frames 2 and 6 are DOWN / RECOIL poses with bent knees. Frames 3 and 7 are NARROW PASSING poses: BOTH BOOTS VERY CLOSE TOGETHER under the hips, one raised foot crossing the standing leg. Frames 4 and 8 are UP poses, one knee visibly raised forward, supporting leg nearly straight. The scarf and cape follow the same rhythmic eight-frame step. Same head size, exact body center and baseline in every equal cell. Transparent background with alpha=0 in empty areas. No shadows, no scenery, no blur, no text, no weapon. Actual walking with alternating visible leg silhouettes, not only cloak changes.

Edit target: attached SIX-column FOUR-row monster animation atlas. This is BACKGROUND EXTRACTION ONLY. Remove the entire purple/brown gradient background and any halos or ground glow so every empty pixel is fully transparent (alpha=0). Preserve every monster pixel, their colors, poses, positions, the exact 6x4 equal-cell layout and the entire original canvas size. The monsters must remain completely opaque with crisp pixel-art edges, including their dark body outlines and tendrils. Do not add or remove monsters. Do not change their frames or geometry. No checkerboard painted into the picture, no shadows or decorative backdrop, no ground. Output a genuine transparent PNG atlas ready to overlay directly on a game arena.
integration: PNGs originais preservados. AtlasTexture/SpriteFrames referenciam regiões e margens alinhadas; nenhum recorte ou reamostragem foi gravado nas imagens.
